messages:
leah.ross: Hey team, day 1 checklist hiccup. Trying to enroll my security key in Okta and Edge keeps saying 'No security key found'. Also the onboarding Drive link opened my personal Google account and shows 'Request access' (I have two Google profiles). Who do I bug?
it-help: Welcome @leah.ross! For keys: @it-identity or IT oncall. Quick Q: Windows or Mac? VPN connected? Which browser?
leah.ross: Windows 11, latest Edge, I am on company VPN (GlobalProtect). Key is YubiKey 5 NFC. I did try without VPN and same result.
it-identity: Two common issues: 1) Browser profile conflicts (personal vs corp Google) can cause Drive weirdness. 2) Some VPNs/proxies interfere with WebAuthn/U2F traffic. Can you try an Edge InPrivate window and also check edge://settings/content/securityKeys to ensure sites are allowed?
leah.ross: InPrivate didn't help. I checked edge settings, the site doesn't appear in blocked list. Okta modal just loops with 'No security key found'.
matt-devex: Sometimes Edge has a legacy U2F fallback enabled/disabled; for modern keys we need WebAuthn. Also if you have a Chrome extension that mungs credential flows (privacy extensions), disable them.
leah.ross: Disabled extensions, rebooted. Still loops. Any debug logs I can paste?
it-help: Can you run PowerShell to list USB devices and paste output?
```
Get-PnpDevice -FriendlyName '*Yubi*' | Format-List
```
leah.ross: Shows Yubico YubiKey 5 under USB devices.
it-identity: Hardware visible. Next try: temporarily disconnect VPN and register the key (not just try, fully disconnect). Also try the YubiKey on a different USB port (avoid hubs).
leah.ross: I fully disconnected VPN and tried direct port -> Okta still didn't pick it up. I noticed Edge shows multiple profiles; maybe Okta session is under personal profile?
matt-devex: If you have both Google accounts signed-in in the browser, Okta might be using the wrong account for SSO. Try single-sign-on flow in a fresh InPrivate window and ensure you complete the corporate Google sign-in first.
leah.ross: Did that and the Okta login flowed via corp Google. This time when I clicked 'Register security key' Edge asked for device access, I touched the key, but still got 'Registration failed' after the touch. Error text: 'Registration failed: 0x801c'.
it-help: 0x801c sometimes maps to a WebAuthn timeout when requests are proxied. Are you on split-tunnel disabled (i.e., all traffic through corp proxy)?
leah.ross: Yes, company VPN forces all traffic through proxy. I can test from home network later but prefer to get it working now.
it-identity: I can temporarily provision a backup method so you can finish onboarding. Meanwhile, I'll run a quick check on our Okta settings for your org unit. Any chance your YubiKey firmware is older? You can check firmware via YubiKey Manager (ykman).
leah.ross: I don't have ykman installed.
matt-devex: If you're open to a faster workaround: we'll share the Drive folder directly to your corp email and send a 1Password invite again. That gets you unstuck while we dig into WebAuthn. Also try registering via a phone (NFC) if your key + phone support it.
leah.ross: Phone NFC didn't work. Ok thanks, please share the Drive.
okta-bot: Okta: Activation link sent to leah@redwood.com at 1764509600.
it-identity: Done — I shared the onboarding Drive folder directly to your corp account and resent the 1Password invite. I also requested an exception to allow WebAuthn traf to bypass proxy for your client IP for 1 hour to test. Let me know when you try again.
leah.ross: I accepted the Drive share and got 1Password invite. Thanks! Trying key register now with the temporary bypass...
leah.ross: Success — Okta accepted the key after the bypass. Looks like the proxy was blocking WebAuthn traffic.
it-identity: Good catch. We'll update our VPN/proxy rules to allow the necessary endpoints for WebAuthn flows. For now, policy is to store MFA recovery codes in the company 1Password vault (see #eng-security). If you have any personal backup, keep it separate.
leah.ross: Saved codes in the company vault. One more: I had earlier an invite go to my personal email (I sometimes forward). Any tips to avoid that?
matt-devex: Best practice: sign into your corporate Google profile before clicking invites. If you accidentally accept with personal, sign out and use the corp profile, then re-request access. If an invite lands in personal, ask IT to re-send to corporate address.
leah.ross: Got it. Appreciate the help everyone! Closing this thread. :tada:
